Dear Sir:
Re Executive Order 11644 Draft Environmental Statement
on Off-road Vehicles
I am the president of the Denver Region Geologists Society, a group composed of minerals exploration people from the Denver area and representing a broad cross section of that industry. At our last meeting, we discussed the Draft Environmental Statement on Order 11644. It is our contention that the Draft Environmental Statement appears to take very little notice of the needs of the mining and mining exploration industries. The society has, therefore, asked me to respectfully bring to your attention the great importance of access to our industry. We believe that the mining industry is cooperating to as high a degree as possible with the various and extensive legislation and rules which have come into effect recently with regard to travel in the forests. Such travel in our case is not simply for recreational purposes, but is indeed an absolute and integral part of the business of exploring for new mineral deposits. I am sure that you are aware of the great importance of the mining industry to this country, and can only ask that this importance be taken into account in the creation of rules, regulations and restrictions under this new executive order.
DREGS is ready to cooperate in any way possible to preserve our environment within a framework which will allow the continuing development of a healthy mining industry. We ask only that proper consideration be given to the needs of all groups involved.
Sincerely,
39
DENVER REGION EXPLORATION GEOLOGISTS
A. L. White, Ph.D.
President
